message.content: {"caption":"A workflow diagram shows how Alita turns a question into an output by coordinating an agent, creating and packaging tools, and feeding them back into an iterative loop.","description":"The diagram is organized around a large dashed, rounded rectangular cycle labeled “CodeReAct Loop.” Its perimeter arrows point right along the top, down the right side, left along the bottom, and up the left side. A plug icon sits near the upper-left corner, a server icon at the upper-right, a chat-bubble icon at the lower-left, and crossed tools at the lower-right, visually suggesting connectivity, services, communication, and tooling around the cycle. At the top, a pink “Question” box with a person and question/document symbols has a red arrow pointing down to the “Manager Agent,” drawn as a person with documents inside a gray cloud. The Manager Agent connects to the blue-cloud “Web Agent,” illustrated with a person and webpage; a blue double-headed arrow between them indicates two-way communication. A short gray horizontal connector links the Manager Agent to the tool-creation area. A green arrow points down from the Manager Agent to a green “Output” box containing a person and an orange check mark. The central gray rounded panel is labeled “MCP Creation” and contains a pink “MCP Brainstorming” block illustrated with tools and a light bulb. A magenta arrow leads right from brainstorming to a layered yellow process block, which contains three labeled activities with icons: “Open-source Searching,” “Script Generating,” and “Virtual Env Execution.” A yellow right-pointing arrow leads from this process to a package/tool illustration labeled “Encapsulate,” followed by a gray right-pointing arrow into the purple-cloud “MCP Box.” The box contains a toolbox and tool symbols, including a paperclip, indicating stored tools. A purple feedback path labeled “Self Evolving” runs from the MCP Box leftward along the bottom and then curves upward, with its arrow pointing toward the Manager Agent. Thus, the diagram depicts question-to-agent processing, agent collaboration with the Web Agent, tool brainstorming and creation, encapsulation into the MCP Box, and feedback to the Manager Agent before output.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
